svg.title: Context Layer protocol map
svg.desc: An interactive architecture map for a user-owned context layer: ingestion, vault, policy gates, scoped bundles, interface surfaces, discovery, and receipt rail.

g.data-summary: A protocol layer for moving useful context between apps, agents, and discovery systems without exposing the raw user vault by default.

text.tspan: A portable protocol layer for sharing useful context with apps, agents, and discovery
without handing over the user's raw vault by default.

g.data-summary: The substrate the context layer can ride on: web standards, social protocols, storage protocols, agent protocols, and payment rails.
The channels where source events arrive before they are normalized into the vault. Some are standards, some are app or device protocols.

text.tspan: web · APIs · BLE mesh · Signal · BitChat · files · audio · email

g.data-summary: Turns incoming signals into timestamped events. Examples: message received, file imported, browser page clipped, payment receipt, voice note, device ping.
Maps different event shapes into stable schemas. Example: email, chat, and browser clips all become source events with consistent actor/time/content fields.
Pulls structured objects out of normalized events: entities, relationships, claims, embeddings, time ranges, locations, commitments, and contradictions.
The private store that keeps memory, provenance, identity, policy, and summaries under user control. External systems request scoped context instead of raw vault reads.
The private store that keeps memory, provenance, identity, policy, and summaries under user control. External systems request scoped context instead of raw vault reads.

line.data-summary: A request for context to leave the vault. It must name purpose, recipient/tool, requested fields, retention window, and what receipt will be written.

g.data-summary: The explicit decision point for what can leave the vault. Defined by scope, consent, purpose, expiration, identity, requested task, and receipt requirements.

text.tspan: scope · consent · purpose · expiration · decides what may leave the vault

g.data-summary: The outbound gate. It redacts, aliases, compresses, and routes context so agents receive only what they need for a task.
Matches external opportunities or people against private context without exposing the vault. It returns only the minimum reveal required to continue.
A task-ready packet containing only approved context, AGENTS.md-style instructions, MCP manifests, tool limits, and receipt requirements.

text.tspan: task-ready packet · AGENTS.md · MCP manifests · scoped instructions

g.data-summary: Untrusted means the source is outside the user's authority boundary. Examples: public search results, relays, third-party APIs, strangers, stale pages, and scraped profiles.

path.data-summary: The smallest useful disclosure needed to advance a match. Example: share an anonymized skill range, not the full work history or private notes.

g.data-summary: Where agents, UI, and user experience consume approved bundles. The interface should show provenance, permissions, and receipt state where decisions happen.
Execution environments that use scoped bundles: local agents, cloud agents, model calls, workflow runners, and tool adapters.
The bundle describes the task and available data; the UI chooses suitable surfaces such as cards, tables, maps, timelines, and workspaces.
Agent-suggested writes are proposals, not automatic truth. They return through policy, provenance checks, contradiction handling, and user approval where required.

text.tspan: agent-suggested write routed back through policy

g.data-summary: End-user surfaces built from scoped context: chat, search, social views, browser overlays, voice, AR, and automations.

text.tspan: chat · search · social · browser · voice · AR · automations

path.data-summary: Agent-suggested writes are proposals, not automatic truth. They return through policy, provenance checks, contradiction handling, and user approval where required.

g.data-summary: Append-only receipts for sensitive operations: capture, normalize, extract, policy decisions, proxy operations, bundle creation, model calls, UI surfaces, and external calls.
Policy and proxy components that decide what enters or leaves the vault and how much is revealed.
Private context, summaries, provenance, identity, policy bindings, scoped bundles, and the receipts rail.

text.tspan: vault interior: context bundle + receipts rail

g.data-summary: Dashed lines show operations that write durable audit receipts.

text.tspan: receipt write: sensitive operations write to rail

g.data-summary: Dashed boxes show sources outside the user's trust boundary that must pass through gates before touching private context.
